results.description: In the convergence rate experiment with Gaussian measurements, s = 40, and m = 1125, IRLS exhibits empirical quadratic convergence within a few iterations (around 10), whereas SPF and RiemAdaIHT clearly only exhibit linear convergence.
results.evidence: File: results/formal/convergence_20260905/metrics.csv (config: n1=256, n2=40, r=5, s=40, m=1125, dense Gaussian — matches claim). Final errors: IRLS-LRRS avg=0.749, SPF avg=0.997, RiemAdaIHT avg=0.636. (1) Ranking violation: RiemAdaIHT (0.636) beats IRLS (0.749) — the required order IRLS > RiemAdaIHT does not hold. (2) Quadratic convergence claim unsupported: IRLS relative_change per iteration is INCREASING (0.092→0.127, ratios ~1.02–1.09 per step), showing no convergence at all, not quadratic convergence. RiemAdaIHT relative_change decreases consistently (0.322→0.055, ratios ~0.73–0.84), showing linear convergence as stated in the paper for it, but IRLS does NOT outperform it on the error metric.
results.note: The CSV uses method name 'IRLS-LRRS' (not 'IRLS'), but config and context confirm this is the IRLS method in the claim. The metric column 'relative_change' appears to capture per-iteration step size, not relative Frobenius error to the true solution; 'final_error' captures the terminal relative Frobenius error. Neither metric supports the claim.

results.description: The median relative Frobenius reconstruction error of IRLS, SPF, and RiemAdaIHT is roughly proportional to the inverse square root of the signal-to-noise ratio (SNR).
results.evidence:
Run outputs found in results/formal/noise_20260905/metrics.csv (27 rows, SNR ∈ {10, 1000, 1000000}, 3 seeds each). Computed median relative Frobenius errors per method per SNR:

IRLS-LRRS: SNR=10 → 0.9851, SNR=1000 → 0.9835, SNR=1e6 → 0.9834. Ratios (SNR10→1000, 1000→1e6): 0.9984, 0.9999. Expected ~0.1 for 1/sqrt(SNR) scaling — observed ratio is ~1 (no scaling).

RiemAdaIHT: SNR=10 → 0.9560, SNR=1000 → 0.9540, SNR=1e6 → 0.9538. Ratios: 0.9979, 0.9998. Again essentially constant — no 1/sqrt(SNR) dependence.

SPF: SNR=10 → 0.4161, SNR=1000 → 0.0442, SNR=1e6 → 0.0351. Ratio SNR10→1000: 0.106 (consistent with 1/sqrt(SNR)), but ratio SNR1000→1e6: 0.793 (far from 0.1). Inconsistent.

All three methods fail to show 1/sqrt(SNR) scaling consistently. IRLS and RiemAdaIHT produce near-constant errors (~0.98 and ~0.95) regardless of SNR, indicating they are not converging to the signal. The experiment also only covers SNR up to 1e6, not the 10 to 10^12 range stated in the claim.
results.note: The config shows seeds: [0, 1] but the CSV contains 3 seeds (0, 1, 2). The SNR range is limited to {10, 1000, 1e6} versus the claimed 10 to 10^12. The near-unity errors for IRLS and RiemAdaIHT suggest algorithmic failure (non-convergence), so the 1/sqrt(SNR) claim cannot be verified from these outputs.

results.description: IRLS is as noise robust as SPF and RiemAdaIHT, achieving reconstruction error of the order of the noise norm.
results.evidence: results/formal/noise_20260905/metrics.csv: IRLS-LRRS has relative_error ≈ 0.983 (mean across seeds) at SNR=10, 0.983 at SNR=1000, and 0.983 at SNR=1,000,000. The error/noise_norm ratio grows to ~1000 at SNR=1,000,000 (noise_norm≈0.001 but error≈0.983), showing IRLS does NOT achieve error of the order of the noise norm. RiemAdaIHT behaves similarly (relative_error ≈ 0.951 across all SNR, ratio ~1000 at high SNR). SPF actually does improve with SNR (mean error drops from 0.557 at SNR=10 to 0.058 at SNR=1000), contradicting the claim that all three are equally noise-robust. IRLS is far worse than SPF at high SNR, not comparable.
results.note: The run outputs for exp10_noise_robustness (noise_20260905) directly contradict the claim. IRLS errors remain flat near ~0.983 regardless of noise level, which means it is NOT noise-robust and does NOT achieve reconstruction error of the order of the noise norm. SPF outperforms both IRLS and RiemAdaIHT at higher SNR, so the "equally robust" comparison also fails.
